description: Cross-harness matrix suite for the messaging plugin's 9 skills (aws-sqs-sns, azure-service-bus, gcp-pubsub, kafka, nats, overview, pulsar, rabbitmq, redis-streams). Prompts are deliberately neutral (no mention of a skills library or docs) so the no-skill arm is not tipped off. Every expected answer is traceable to cited content shipped in each skill's SKILL.md on 2026-08-09. knowledge: 'recent' = fact a bare model plausibly lacks (specific limit, version-gated feature, niche number); 'stable' = long-standing or widely-known fact a strong bare model may already know.

tasks.prompt: For an SQS FIFO queue running in high throughput mode, what is the maximum number of transactions per second the queue can handle? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/aws-sqs-sns/SKILL.md - SQS FIFO section: High-throughput mode up to 70,000 transactions/s

tasks.prompt: What is the maximum number of in-flight, not yet deleted, messages a single standard SQS queue supports? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/aws-sqs-sns/SKILL.md - SQS Standard section: 120,000 in-flight message limit

tasks.prompt: Can an SNS FIFO topic deliver messages to a standard, non-FIFO SQS queue as a subscriber? Answer in one sentence.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/aws-sqs-sns/SKILL.md - SNS FIFO Topics: strict ordering and exactly-once to SQS FIFO subscriptions only

tasks.prompt: In Azure Service Bus, what is the default maximum delivery count for a queue before a message is automatically dead-lettered? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/azure-service-bus/SKILL.md - Queues section: Max delivery count default 10

tasks.prompt: What is the maximum number of subscriptions a single Azure Service Bus topic can have? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/azure-service-bus/SKILL.md - Topics and Subscriptions section: up to 2,000 subscriptions per topic

tasks.prompt: On the Premium tier of Azure Service Bus, using AMQP, what is the maximum message size supported? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/azure-service-bus/SKILL.md - Premium Tier section: messages up to 100 MB (AMQP only)

tasks.prompt: What is the maximum message retention duration you can configure on a Google Cloud Pub/Sub topic? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/gcp-pubsub/SKILL.md - Topics section: message retention (10 min to 31 days)

tasks.prompt: For a Pub/Sub dead-letter topic, what is the maximum number of delivery attempts you can configure before a message is forwarded to it? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/gcp-pubsub/SKILL.md - Dead-Letter Topics section: forwarded after 5-100 delivery attempts

tasks.prompt: When publishing to a Pub/Sub topic using an ordering key, what is the per-key publish throughput limit that can create a hot-key bottleneck? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/gcp-pubsub/SKILL.md - Anti-Patterns table: hot keys block progress, 1 MBps per key limit

tasks.prompt: In which Apache Kafka release did Share Groups, providing queue-like semantics without partition binding, reach general availability? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/kafka/SKILL.md - Share Groups section: GA in Kafka 4.2; preview in 4.1; EA in 4.0

tasks.prompt: Before Share Groups became generally available in Kafka, in which earlier release were they available as a preview feature? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/kafka/SKILL.md - Share Groups section: GA in Kafka 4.2; preview in 4.1; EA in 4.0

tasks.prompt: Does Apache Kafka natively support message priority the way some traditional brokers do? Answer in one sentence.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/kafka/SKILL.md - Kafka vs Traditional Brokers table: Message priority Not supported for Kafka

tasks.prompt: In NATS JetStream, what is the default duration of the message deduplication window used to detect duplicate publishes? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/nats/SKILL.md - Anti-Patterns table: keep Duplicates window as short as practical, default 2min

tasks.prompt: Which NATS server release introduced atomic batch publish and distributed counters? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/nats/SKILL.md - version gates list: atomic batch publish, distributed counters, delayed scheduling, mirror promotion (2.12)

tasks.prompt: For a NATS cluster, why should you use an odd number of nodes such as 3 or 5 rather than an even number? Answer in one sentence.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/nats/SKILL.md - Anti-Patterns table: even-sized clusters risk split-brain; use odd node counts (3 or 5)

tasks.prompt: For event-driven architectures spanning a message broker and external systems, is achieving true exactly-once delivery generally considered practical? Answer in one sentence.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/overview/SKILL.md - Messaging Principles 1: true exactly-once across broker and external systems is impractical

tasks.prompt: Among the major cloud providers, does Google Cloud offer a distinct native point-to-point queue service separate from its pub/sub offering? Answer in one sentence.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/overview/SKILL.md - Cloud provider alignment table: GCP native queue column is blank; Pub/Sub handles both queue and pub/sub patterns

tasks.prompt: For a workload that needs sub-millisecond, fire-and-forget message delivery, which messaging technology is typically recommended? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/overview/SKILL.md - Decision Framework Step 5: sub-millisecond, fire-and-forget -> NATS Core

tasks.prompt: Which Apache Pulsar subscription type delivers messages to many consumers while preserving ordering per key, with individual acknowledgment? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/pulsar/SKILL.md - Subscription Types table: Key_Shared, many consumers per-key, individual ack, per-entity ordering

tasks.prompt: For a non-persistent topic in Apache Pulsar, where is the message data actually stored? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/pulsar/SKILL.md - Topic Types section: Non-persistent topics are broker memory only

tasks.prompt: What does the Pulsar feature called KoP provide? Answer in one sentence.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/pulsar/SKILL.md - intro bullet list: KoP (Kafka-on-Pulsar protocol compatibility)

tasks.prompt: As of which RabbitMQ release does Khepri become the default metadata store for brand-new deployments? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/rabbitmq/SKILL.md - Khepri Metadata Store section: default for new deployments in 4.2

tasks.prompt: What is the default delivery limit, meaning number of redeliveries, before a RabbitMQ quorum queue dead-letters a message? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/rabbitmq/SKILL.md - Quorum Queue Essentials section: default delivery limit 20 redeliveries before dead-lettering

tasks.prompt: In a 7-node RabbitMQ cluster, how many replicas does a quorum queue get by default? Do all 7 nodes hold a copy? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/rabbitmq/SKILL.md - Quorum Queue Essentials table: 7 cluster nodes -> default replicas 3 (not all 7)

tasks.prompt: Does Redis Streams provide exactly-once processing guarantees out of the box? Answer in one sentence.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/redis-streams/SKILL.md - comparison table: Exactly-once No (at-least-once with XACK) for Redis Streams

tasks.prompt: In a Redis Streams consumer group, what is the name of the internal structure that tracks messages delivered but not yet acknowledged? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/redis-streams/SKILL.md - Redis Streams as a Message Broker section: unacknowledged messages tracked in Pending Entries List (PEL)

tasks.prompt: Which Redis Streams command would you use to reassign messages that are stuck pending on a consumer that has failed? Answer concisely.
tasks.notes: plugins/messaging/skills/redis-streams/SKILL.md - Redis Streams as a Message Broker section: XCLAIM and XAUTOCLAIM reassign stuck messages from failed consumers
